NNI should remain the primary direct public-market candidate for the student-loan servicing rails node because its Department of Education servicing exposure is disclosed and material.

The strongest direct underfollowed candidates are Nelnet and Maximus: both sit closer to the operational/regulatory chokepoint than generic education providers. SLM is a direct private-education-loan asset owner and product leader. SoFi is included as a higher-attention reference name because student-loan refinancing volume is explicitly disclosed and tied to federal repayment dynamics, but its broader fintech exposure makes it less pure. Layer 1B expands the universe around student-finance servicing and compliance rails, with emphasis on scarce operational/regulatory infrastructure rather than education providers. The strongest direct public-market mappings found are Nelnet and Maximus, both tied to student-loan servicing or Federal Student Aid operational contracts. Sallie Mae is included as a reference/direct education-finance name because its private student-loan origination, servicing, securitization, and compliance exposure are material. Global Payments is a lower-confidence underfollowed infrastructure hypothesis through ECSI, a wholly owned subsidiary that provides campus-based student-loan servicing, tuition payment plans, refund management, tax-document services, call-center and outsourcing services; exposure materiality to GPN must be verified.
